samples.summary: Two competing cursor policies for the same slide-removal event: the thumbnail panel's Delete slide picks the first SURVIVOR AFTER the anchor, the new heal picks the slide BEFORE the vanished index
samples.evidence: packages/slides/src/view/editor/thumbnail-panel.ts:302-323 does `store.batch(() => store.removeSlides(...))` and only then `editor.setCurrentSlide(nextCurrent)`. Store notification is synchronous at the end of the batch (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:628 `finally { ...; this.notifyChange(); }`), and the frontend's subscriber renders immediately (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1053 `store.onChange(() => { editor.markDirty(); editor.render(); ... })`). So `resolveCurrentSlide` heals to the PREVIOUS slide, fires `currentSlideListeners` (presence broadcast at slides-view.tsx:1073-1080, thumbnail highlight at thumbnail-panel.ts:622) and clears the selection, and only afterwards the panel's `setCurrentSlide` moves the cursor to its intended successor — one delete now emits two current-slide changes/broadcasts landing on different slides. Fix could be in the panel (move the cursor before removing) or in the new heal.

samples.summary: `setStore` does not reset the new `currentIndex`, so a heal right after a store swap clamps against an index belonging to the previous store
samples.evidence: packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:1605-1625 (`setStore`, used by `enterLayoutEditMode`/`exitLayoutEditMode` at 1627-1635 and driven from packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1191/1216) reassigns `this.currentId` but never touches `this.currentIndex`. In layout-edit mode the store serves exactly one synthetic slide (packages/slides/src/store/layout-edit-store.ts:71-78), so `currentIndex` becomes 0; if the first resolve after exiting is a miss (peer deleted the restored slide), the heal lands on slide index 0 rather than near where the user actually was. Same the other direction: a stale large index clamps to the deck tail.

samples.summary: Healing happens only on the paint paths; every other consumer of `currentId`/`getCurrentSlideId()` can still observe (or write to) a dangling id between the mutation and the next frame
samples.evidence: `getCurrentSlideId()` (editor.ts:1487) returns the raw field, and non-paint sites were not routed through `resolveCurrentSlide`: `insertTable` writes with the unvalidated `this.currentId` (editor.ts:1780-1781), `previewAnimations` (editor.ts:2668), `currentSlide()` (editor.ts:5590-5593), PageUp/PageDown navigation bails on `currentIdx === -1` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:573-583), and thumbnail arrow navigation does the same (packages/slides/src/view/editor/thumbnail-panel.ts:642-643). In hosts without a synchronous render-on-change (harness/tests/mobile paths) these stay inert or target a removed slide until something paints.

samples.summary: Hunt-harness doc comment and refusal text still describe the pre-fix behaviour this change removes (issue #883)
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts:284-315 asserts "the editor legitimately points at a slide the store no longer has, because undo removed it" and refuses in that state; `slides.currentSlideIndex` (bridge.ts:665-669) documents a `null` index as the same signal. With the heal in place that state is transient (or gone) on rendered hosts, so both the comment and the documented reader contract now describe old behaviour.

samples.summary: `render()` is no longer side-effect-free: it can now clear selection, cancel text editing, discard a crop session and notify listeners — and it is called synchronously from a store-change callback
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1059 calls `editor.render()` directly inside `store.onChange`. The heal path (editor.ts:1544-1554) re-enters `exitEditMode('cancel')` → `finishEditMode()` → `render()`/`repaintOverlay()` (editor.ts:4576-4591) and fires `currentSlideListeners`, whose frontend handler writes presence back into the store (`broadcast` → `store.updatePresence`, slides-view.tsx:1073-1080). Callers that assumed painting cannot mutate editor/store state (this one, board-view.tsx:557/717, mobile-slides-view.tsx:389, refitCanvas at slides-view.tsx:872-873) were not reviewed for that re-entrancy; `updatePresence` only guards the in-batch case (yorkie-slides-store.ts:2748-2752), so I could not confirm every notify path lands outside an open `doc.update`. Also note uncommitted text is discarded here while every other cursor-move path (`setCurrentSlide` editor.ts:1494, `setStore` editor.ts:1606) commits.

finding.summary: `render()` is no longer side-effect-free: it can now clear selection, cancel text editing, discard a crop session and notify listeners — and it is called synchronously from a store-change callback
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1059 calls `editor.render()` directly inside `store.onChange`. The heal path (editor.ts:1544-1554) re-enters `exitEditMode('cancel')` → `finishEditMode()` → `render()`/`repaintOverlay()` (editor.ts:4576-4591) and fires `currentSlideListeners`, whose frontend handler writes presence back into the store (`broadcast` → `store.updatePresence`, slides-view.tsx:1073-1080). Callers that assumed painting cannot mutate editor/store state (this one, board-view.tsx:557/717, mobile-slides-view.tsx:389, refitCanvas at slides-view.tsx:872-873) were not reviewed for that re-entrancy; `updatePresence` only guards the in-batch case (yorkie-slides-store.ts:2748-2752), so I could not confirm every notify path lands outside an open `doc.update`. Also note uncommitted text is discarded here while every other cursor-move path (`setCurrentSlide` editor.ts:1494, `setStore` editor.ts:1606) commits.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. slides-view.tsx:1051-1059 does call editor.markDirty() then editor.render() synchronously inside store.onChange. render() reaches the heal: editor.ts:1427 calls resolveCurrentSlide(doc) (the clean-frame early return at editor.ts:1413-1420 is bypassed by the preceding markDirty()). The heal at editor.ts:1544-1554 mutates currentId/currentIndex, calls exitImageCrop(false), exitEditMode('cancel'), setCellSelection(null), selection.clear(), and then fires currentSlideListeners. exitEditMode('cancel') routes to finishEditMode() (editor.ts:4338-4340), which fires textEditingListeners and re-enters render()/repaintOverlay() (editor.ts:4584-4590) — a paint nested inside a paint. The notify lands in the frontend: slides-view.tsx:1094 subscribes onCurrentSlideChange(broadcast) and broadcast calls store.updatePresence at slides-view.tsx:1079. updatePresence (yorkie-slides-store.ts:2748-2752) only folds into activePresence when a batch's doc.update is open; on the remote-change path notifyChange() is invoked from inside the doc.subscribe callback (yorkie-slides-store.ts:364-367), so the else branch opens a doc.update re-entrantly from Yorkie's event dispatch with no guard I could find. Other unreviewed callers of the now-side-effecting render() also exist: board-view.tsx:557 (inside store.onChange, whose onSelectionChange at board-view.tsx:568-572 issues doc.update, so a heal-driven selection.clear() writes presence mid-dispatch), board-view.tsx:717, mobile-slides-view.tsx:389, slides-view.tsx:872-873 and slides-view.tsx:1115. This is an invariant violation affecting consumers outside the diff — squarely in the blast-radius lane — and the most likely trigger (a peer deleting the slide the user is on) arrives through exactly the remote-change onChange path. No guard renders it unreachable and nothing about it is out of scope, so it stands.

finding.summary: Thumbnail-panel delete now double-moves the cursor: the heal fires first (backwards) and its own survivor choice (forwards) second
finding.evidence: thumbnail-panel.ts:320-323 does `store.batch(() => store.removeSlides([...targetIds]))` and only afterwards `editor.setCurrentSlide(nextCurrent)`. The batch notifies store listeners synchronously, and packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1053 responds with `editor.markDirty(); editor.render();` — which now runs `resolveCurrentSlide` and heals the cursor to `currentIndex - 1` (the slide BEFORE the deleted one), firing `currentSlideListeners` (presence broadcast at slides-view.tsx:1073-1094, thumbnail highlight, notes panel, toolbar refresh) and clearing selection. Line 321-322 then moves the cursor a second time to the panel's intended survivor (the first surviving slide AFTER the anchor, lines 315-318). Net effect for the user: a visible one-frame jump to the wrong slide, two `onCurrentSlideChange` notifications and two presence writes per delete. The delete path should either be made heal-aware or the heal should reuse the same survivor rule.

verdict.reason: The described code and chain exist exactly as claimed. thumbnail-panel.ts:320 mutates the store before fixing the cursor at 321-323; YorkieSlidesStore.batch (yorkie-slides-store.ts:598-630) and MemoryStore.batch (memory.ts:1789-1803) both call notifyChange() synchronously before returning; slides-view.tsx:1051-1053 responds with editor.markDirty(); editor.render(), and markDirty (editor.ts:2640) defeats render()'s dirty short-circuit (editor.ts:1413-1420) so resolveCurrentSlide runs at editor.ts:1427. With currentId deleted, the heal (editor.ts:1533-1555) moves the cursor to clamp(currentIndex-1) — the slide BEFORE the deleted one — clears selection/cell selection and fires currentSlideListeners, which include the presence broadcast (slides-view.tsx:1073-1094 wired at :1094). Control then returns to thumbnail-panel.ts:321 where nextCurrent (first surviving slide AFTER the anchor, lines 315-318) differs from the healed id for any current-slide delete at index > 0, so setCurrentSlide (editor.ts:1491-1504, whose only guard is currentId === id) moves the cursor a second time and fires the listeners again. Net: one-frame jump to the wrong slide plus duplicate onCurrentSlideChange/presence writes. No guard anywhere suppresses the heal for locally-initiated removals. This is in the blast-radius lane (behaviour change to resolveCurrentSlide leaving an out-of-diff caller inconsistent) and is major impact.
